subject: Numeracy
title: Counting to 5 and back
objectives: Children will count objects to 5 touching each one once.
Children will recognise the numerals 1 to 5.
content: Counting objects to 5, counting rhymes, and the numerals 1 to 5.
teachingActivities: Always count real objects that children can touch and move; model touching each object once and moving it aside; say the last number as how many; link numerals to quantities; use the first week to observe how far each child counts.
learnerActivities: Count up to 5 objects touching each once and match numerals 1 to 5 to quantities.
resources: Counters such as bottle tops, stones or seeds
assessment: Observe whether each child counts up to 5 objects accurately and matches a numeral to a group.

lessons.title: Counting to five
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count up to five objects touching each once.
successCriteria: Touches each object once while counting
Says the last number as how many
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children arrive able to count a little, usually to about five, and to use words such as big and small.
lessons.starter: Show five bottle tops in a line and say "Let us count them together. One, two, three, four, five."
teacherActivities: Count five bottle tops slowly, touching and moving each one.
Say "How many?" and point to the last bottle top.
Give each child a small group of up to five counters.
Walk around and ask each child "How many do you have?"
learnerActivities: Children count aloud with the teacher.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count five bottle tops slowly, touching and moving each one. Children: Children count aloud with the teacher.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "How many?" and point to the last bottle top. Children: Children say five.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a small group of up to five counters. Children: Child counts their counters.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk around and ask each child "How many do you have?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Count and move
steps: Touch each one and move it to a plate.
practical.safety: Use counters larger than a child’s fist so they cannot be swallowed and supervise closely. Do not let children put counters in their mouths.

differentiation.support: Count one to three objects with the child, guiding the touching hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count out exactly five and then say one more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many counters do you have?
What do we say last?
questions.expected: The last number is how many.

expectedOutcomes: Counts up to five objects accurately
Says how many in a group
lessons.conclusion: Hold up five fingers and say "Five. Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Count five spoons or five stones with your child at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count up to five objects touching each once" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting rhymes to five
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sing counting rhymes and show the numbers with fingers.
successCriteria: Sings a counting rhyme with actions
Shows the right number of fingers
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children arrive able to count a little, usually to about five, and to use words such as big and small.
resources: Rhyme pictures: five little monkeys, five fat sausages
lessons.starter: Sing "One, two, three, four, five, once I caught a fish alive" with finger actions.
teacherActivities: Teach the rhyme line by line with finger actions.
Sing the rhyme again and count down from five.
Use finger puppets to act out a rhyme.
Ask "How many are left?" at each verse.
learnerActivities: Children copy the lines and fingers.
Children hold up the right number of fingers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Teach the rhyme line by line with finger actions. Children: Children copy the lines and fingers.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the rhyme again and count down from five. Children: Children hold up the right number of fingers.
Step 3. Teacher: Use finger puppets to act out a rhyme. Children: Child moves puppets and counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many are left?" at each verse. Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Rhyme and fingers
practical.safety: Keep the movement small and seated to avoid collisions. Make sure children have space around them.

differentiation.support: Sing slowly and show the fingers beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a verse and say the numbers backwards.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many fingers on one hand?

expectedOutcomes: Sings a counting rhyme with actions
lessons.conclusion: Sing the rhyme once more and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing counting rhymes at bedtime and count fingers.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing counting rhymes and show the numbers with fingers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: One, two, three, four, five, once I caught a fish alive.

lessons.title: Numerals 1 to 5
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will recognise and name the numerals 1 to 5.
successCriteria: Matches a numeral to a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children arrive able to count a little, usually to about five, and to use words such as big and small.
lessons.starter: Hold up the numeral 3 and say "This is the numeral three. It tells us how many."
teacherActivities: Show each numeral card and say its name.
Place the matching number of counters under each card.
Mix the cards and ask children to find a numeral.
Let each child match a card to a group.
learnerActivities: Child places the card by a group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each numeral card and say its name. Children: Children say each numeral.
Step 2. Teacher: Place the matching number of counters under each card. Children: Children count the counters.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix the cards and ask children to find a numeral. Children: Child points to the numeral.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child match a card to a group. Children: Child places the card by a group.

practical.title: Match numeral and group
steps: Put the card by the group.
practical.safety: Use counters too large to swallow and supervise matching. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Match numerals 1 to 3 only with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put the cards in order from 1 to 5.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Hold up each numeral and say it together.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for numerals 1 to 5 on doors, clocks and calendars.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "recognise and name the numerals 1 to 5" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting out
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count out a number of objects when asked.
successCriteria: Counts out the number asked for
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children arrive able to count a little, usually to about five, and to use words such as big and small.
lessons.starter: Say "I will ask you for some counters. Can you give me three?"
teacherActivities: Ask a child to count out three counters.
Show a numeral card and ask for that many.
Let children ask each other for a number.
learnerActivities: Child asks a friend for a number.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Ask a child to count out three counters. Children: Child counts out three counters.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a numeral card and ask for that many. Children: Child counts out the number.
Step 3. Teacher: Check by counting together. Children: Children count again to check.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children ask each other for a number. Children: Child asks a friend for a number.

practical.title: Give me counters
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise to avoid putting them in mouths. Keep the floor tidy.

differentiation.support: Count out two or three counters together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count out five and then take one away.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Counts out a number of objects
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child for four spoons or five plates at mealtimes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count out a number of objects when asked" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 counting check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how far each child counts and recognises numerals.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children arrive able to count a little, usually to about five, and to use words such as big and small.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting rhyme and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: counting out, numeral match and rhyme.
At each station ask "How many?" and watch.
Record each child’s level and how far they count.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: counting out, numeral match and rhyme. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many?" and watch. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and how far they count. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Counting stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use counters too large to swallow. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use only up to three.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count to ten.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: counts to 5 with one-to-one touch; matches numerals 1 to 5; sings counting rhymes; says how many.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep counting small groups at home every day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how far each child counts and recognises numerals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
